## The Claim

John Stockton reportedly had a resting heart rate near 35 beats per minute — a number cited in profiles as evidence of elite cardiovascular adaptation. Applied to an NBA point guard who played 1,504 regular-season games over 19 seasons, the claim is specific enough to test: if that physiology were consequential, we should be able to find its trace in durability, fatigue-driven shot selection, and late-game efficiency.

This post asks whether that trace is detectable. It uses the same permutation-inference methodology established in the [Diaw post](../diaw-35bpm/index.qmd), applied to the harder case: a longer career with a pre-1996 data gap that limits within-game analysis to Stockton's ages 34–40.

## Within-Game Resilience: 1996–2003 Window (Stockton ages 34–40)

**Data limitation:** BRef play-by-play starts 1996-97. Stockton's first 12 seasons (1984–96) have no quarter data. Outreach to Squared Statistics (Justin Jacobs) for video-reconstructed pre-1996 data is pending; see `data/html_cache/jacobs_outreach.md`.

**Age-regime caveat:** this analysis covers Stockton ages 34–40. A null result in this window does not contradict a peak-workload resilience claim during his prime (ages 22–34). These results and prime-career results are different estimands and should not be conflated.

### Confounders for within-game estimands

| Confounder | Direction | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| Score margin (blowout) | Starters sit; suppresses minutes and compresses estimates | Sensitivity: restricted to games with Q4 margin ≤ 10 |
| Intentional fouling | Inflates FTA in close games; FT% reflects pressure context | FT% (E2) is least-confounded metric |
| Timeout availability | Teams with more timeouts grant more recovery time; unmeasured | Stated explicitly; not mitigated |
| Age regime (34–40) | Later-career Stockton; null ≠ no prime-career effect | Stated explicitly in every result |

---

## What the Data Can and Cannot Say

**Selection bias.** Cohort conditioned on ≥ 600 career games — describes durability among long-career PGs.

**B2B state selection.** Back-to-back comparison is within healthier player-states by construction.

**Causal language.** No result here proves or disproves the 35 BPM figure. The analysis is *consistent with* or *does not contradict* the physiology claim. It does not establish a causal mechanism.

**Pre-1996 gap.** E2/E4/E5 cover 7 of Stockton's 19 seasons. Any claim about his full-career within-game resilience requires either additional data sources or an explicit extrapolation caveat.
